The two halves of that word are swapped by the time PadRead returns it, so 0x1000 is UP and 0x0800 is START. Four independent uses say so: the slot holding 0x0800 is read only by the pause menu, the one holding 0x0100 opens the map, play_movie skips a movie on 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 -- the four face buttons -- and everything on 0x800, and the title menu confirms on 0x20/0x40/0x800 and moves its cursor on 0x1000/0x4000. Under the raw reading those are, in order, R1 opening the menu, L2 the map, the four directions skipping a movie, and the cursor moving on TRIANGLE and CROSS

The first guess, 0x801b2614, reads zero for a whole session and is wrong. POSITIVE IS UP: the resting -190 was read as a downward tilt and the port was built on that, and a player looking up saw it look down

The second steps object_table by 0x44 for 396 slots, skips a u16 type id of 0xff, clears bit 0x80 of +3 every frame and dispatches on the class byte at +4 -- 0xe9 and 0xe5 are skipped, 0x1f, 0xf0 and 0xf2 each have their own path. _note_object_model.name: object type -> model

The 128 was MEASURED, not reasoned: a player stood in the game beside the port and named four pairs off the model gallery -- helmet type 34 = model 162, healing grass 104 = 232, save point 227 = 355, bull's head 253 = 381 -- and all four differ by exactly 128. The sizes agree: the grass is 384x211x416 under the rule where MO.T[type] gave it 4176x4096x3808, which is what the player saw as a big white thing. While the counter at 0x801b2566 runs, 0x80031254 halves it each frame. player_look reads it six times and never writes it

0x801b2566.name: turn_slow_timer
0x801b2566.evidence: a half that player_controller counts down at 0x8003125c, halving player_turn_max each frame while it is non-zero (0x80031254); it also drives a separate ramp on 0x801b24f6 that is bounded at -0xce4

0x801e647c.name: surface_plane_18
0x801e647c.evidence: written only by collision opcode 0x18 (0x80033a2c) and seeded to 100000 at tile_collision's entry; read only by sync_player_pos, which compares surface + 0x640 with the player's eye and calls 0x80030a6c when the eye is past it

0x801e6480.name: surface_plane_19
0x801e6480.evidence: the same, written by collision opcode 0x19 (0x80033a9c)

0x801e6484.name: surface_plane_17
0x801e6484.evidence: the same, written by collision opcode 0x17 (0x80033ac4)

0x801e646e.name: collision_layer_offset
0x801e646e.evidence: 0 or 5, the offset into the cell's ten bytes that tile_collision is reading. Collision opcode 0x40 (0x800339a8) toggles it and restarts the shape on the other layer; no shape in the game uses it

0x80030a6c.name: player_throw
0x80030a6c.evidence: sets player_state to 0x11, plays sound 0x6e through 0x8001576c(6, 0x6e) and, given a pointer, copies six bytes into player_velocity. sync_player_pos calls it when the eye goes under one of the three surface planes; player_vertical_pre and player_move also call it

0x801b2638.name: depth_under_plane_18
0x801b2638.evidence: sync_player_pos: surface_plane_18 + 0x640 less the eye. Below -1000 it calls player_throw

0x801b263c.name: depth_under_plane_19
0x801b263c.evidence: sync_player_pos: surface_plane_19 + 0x640 less the eye. At or below zero it calls player_throw

0x80026fe4.name: frame_begin
0x80026fe4.evidence: flips the byte at 0x801aeae8 between 0 and 1, selects the 12-byte record at 0x80199158 + i*12 into 0x80199170 and the ordering table at 0x80199174 + i*0x8000, then calls ClearOTagR. 36 callers, and the same shape as OPEN.EXE's frame_begin at 0x800133c8

0x800270f8.name: frame_end
0x800270f8.evidence: DrawSync(0), then PutDispEnv(disp_env + i*20) and PutDrawEnv(draw_env + i*92) for the buffer 0x801aeae8 names -- the PSY-Q sizes of DISPENV and DRAWENV, which is what fixes both arrays. 36 callers

0x80027a40.name: pad_wait_release
0x80027a40.evidence: loops on PadRead(1) until the low half is zero -- it waits for every button to be let go, not for one to be pressed. 36 callers, all of them after a menu choice

0x801aeae8.name: draw_buffer_index
0x801aeae8.evidence: 0 or 1, flipped by frame_begin with `sltiu $v0, $v0, 1` and read by frame_end to pick which display and drawing environment to hand the GPU

0x801a9274.name: disp_env
0x801a9274.evidence: two DISPENVs, 20 bytes each: frame_end forms 0x801a9274 + i*20 and passes it to PutDispEnv

0x801a91bc.name: draw_env
0x801a91bc.evidence: two DRAWENVs, 92 bytes each: frame_end forms 0x801a91bc + i*92 and passes it to PutDrawEnv

0x80199174.name: ordering_table
0x80199174.evidence: two ordering tables, 0x8000 bytes each, selected by draw_buffer_index; frame_begin clears the chosen one with ClearOTagR

0x80199170.name: current_draw_slot
0x80199170.evidence: frame_begin writes 0x80199158 + draw_buffer_index*12 here, and the drawing routines read it -- 0x8003f304 takes its +8 for the primitive buffer

0x8002a310.name: award_exp
0x8002a310.evidence: (s16 delta). Adds to player_exp, caps it at 0xf423f = 999999, and while the total reaches player_exp_next and the level byte is below 0xff, takes a level: HP max, MP max, the stat at +0x36 and the next threshold all come out of the 12-byte record at level_table + level*12, the five halfwords at 0x801b2518..0x801b2520 each grow by one if they are not zero and rand() < 0x6665, and everything is clamped to 999. Past the table's 99 records it extrapolates by the difference between the last two. Checked: 13 of 13 RAM snapshots hold what their level's record says

0x8009f114.name: level_table
0x8009f114.evidence: 99 records of 12 bytes -- HP max, MP max, the gain for 0x801b2516, then a u32 of experience for the next level. Past the end of GAME.EXE's image, so it comes off the disc: FDAT.T entry 97 at offset 12592, found by searching every file for the first 36 bytes of the live table. tools/levelup.py reads it

0x801b2516.name: player_stat_36
0x801b2516.evidence: the stat the level table's third column adds to: 20 at level 1 and 21 at level 2, which is the running sum of that column. Clamped to 999 by award_exp like the maxima. What it is called in the game is not established

0x801b2518.name: player_grow_stats
0x801b2518.evidence: five halfwords, 0x801b2518 to 0x801b2520, that award_exp grows by a coin toss on each level -- one added if the stat is not already zero and rand() < 0x6665, about four times in five. 0x801b2520 is player.py's unknown_40, which goes 10 -> 11 between the level 1 and level 2 snapshots. They are the only random part of levelling

0x8007dd08.name: AddPrim
0x8007dd08.evidence: PSY-Q's addPrim, read off the code: takes the low 24 bits of the ordering table entry into the primitive's tag and the primitive's address into the entry, keeping each one's top byte. Two words in, two words out, no call

0x8007de70.name: SetPolyFT4
0x8007de70.evidence: writes 9 into the tag's length byte at +3 and 0x2c into the command byte at +7 -- the word count and the GPU code of a textured, blended four-point polygon. That pair is what names it

0x80027414.name: ui_prim_begin
0x80027414.evidence: takes the primitive buffer from current_draw_slot +8, keeps it at gp+0x160 as the current primitive, calls SetPolyFT4 on it and writes the three colour bytes from gp+0x5c, gp+0x60 and gp+0x64 into its +4, +5 and +6. 14 callers, every one of them a menu

0x80027494.name: ui_prim_quad
0x80027494.evidence: fills the current primitive's four corners at +8, +0x10, +0x18, +0x20 from (x, y, w, h) and the four UV pairs at +0xc, +0x14, +0x1c, +0x24 -- the POLY_FT4 layout exactly

0x80027530.name: ui_prim_add
0x80027530.evidence: AddPrim(ot_pointer + a0*4, the current primitive) -- a0 is the depth the UI quad is filed at

0x801a9174.name: ot_pointer
0x801a9174.evidence: the ordering table ui_prim_add files into: it reads the word here and indexes it by the depth

0x800279a4.name: pad_read_latch
0x800279a4.evidence: PadRead(1), and if anything is held it sets gp+0x34 before returning the word. The latch is what tells a menu that a button has been touched since it opened

0x80016ab8.name: vec_angle
0x80016ab8.evidence: the direction of (a0, a1) in the game's 0x1000-to-the-turn units. It compares |a0| and |a1|, divides the smaller by the larger shifted left 12, hands that to 0x800742ac, and folds the answer into one of the four quadrants with 0x800 and 0xfff. 19 callers, all of them things that turn towards something

0x800742ac.name: arctan_unit
0x800742ac.evidence: vec_angle's only callee: a ratio in 12-bit fixed point to an angle, iterating over the table at 0x8009591c with 0x1000 as its seed

0x801e6474.name: collision_surface
0x801e6474.evidence: the nearest surface tile_collision finds, seeded to 100000 at its entry (0x80032658) and lowered by every floor, ramp and wall handler that the query reaches. player_vertical, player_move, player_horizontal, collide_surface, collide_at_cell and both actor movers read it as the ground height

0x801e6478.name: collision_ceiling
0x801e6478.evidence: the companion slot the wall and ceiling handlers leave the *lower* bound in; player_horizontal reads it at 0x8002e5e0

0x800341e8.name: light_table_reset
0x800341e8.evidence: copies the 0x3f-entry lighting table from 0x80081c8c into tile_look, twice per entry (the near and far copies), at the top of every frame. game_main calls it first in the loop

0x80034180.name: render_flags_reset
0x80034180.evidence: writes the eleven render flags at 0x801aeafa..0x801aeb0c back to their defaults -- 1, 1, 0... and 0xff -- second in game_main's frame

0x80034300.name: light_table_step
0x80034300.evidence: when 0x801aeef8 is set, runs 0x80016290 over all 64 lighting entries three times, once per colour, then clears the flag. The interpolation that makes torchlight move

0x8002b330.name: camera_pose
0x8002b330.evidence: (pos_out, ang_out): writes the eye -- player X, player_y + bob + crouch - 0x640, player Z -- and the three view angles from 0x801b2608/0x260a/0x260c. So 0x640 is the eye above the feet, and sync_player_pos adds the same 0x640 back when it compares the eye with the three surface planes

0x800156bc.name: audio_listener_set
0x800156bc.evidence: copies the camera pose game_main just built into the mirror at 0x801b0a10 with its cell layer, and the angles into 0x801b0a22. Only sound_play_3d reads it, to get the distance and the bearing of a cue

0x80015410.name: sound_play_3d
0x80015410.evidence: (kind, position, ..., radius, range): takes the distance from the listener mirror through game_isqrt, drops the cue when it is past the range, and scales the volume by what is left. The low twelve bits of the first argument are a bearing and 0x8000 is a flag

0x8005bc50.name: ai_driver
0x8005bc50.evidence: walks 128 slots of 0x4c bytes at 0x801b80ec; for each live one it publishes the slot at 0x801ba6f0 and its 24-byte definition at 0x801b77ec + 24*slot[+1] into 0x801ba6ec, counts slot[+0x10] down, and calls actor_ai. Fifth in game_main's frame

0x800568bc.name: actor_ai
0x800568bc.evidence: the 4584-instruction behaviour tick ai_driver calls once per live slot. Reads the player's position and state, rolls rand, asks collide_surface and actor_spot_taken, and writes the player's HP -- so it is where a creature decides and where it hits

0x8005eb20.name: level_overlay_tick
0x8005eb20.evidence: calls through the function pointer at [0x8018fae0]+4 -- the level's own code, FDAT.T entry 3n+2 -- and then owns the fade when a level changes. Seventh in game_main's frame

0x800422b8.name: render_frame
0x800422b8.evidence: the last call in game_main's loop: the camera matrix (0x800357e8), then 0x800351fc, 0x80041f9c, 0x80034bf4, 0x80035630, 0x80043858 and 0x8003df50, then the GPU primitive state for the frame

0x801b80ec.name: ai_slots
0x801b80ec.evidence: 128 slots of 0x4c bytes; ai_driver walks them and byte +0 is 0xff when the slot is free

0x801b77ec.name: ai_defs
0x801b77ec.evidence: 24-byte records ai_driver indexes by a slot's +1 byte and publishes at 0x801ba6ec for actor_ai to read

0x801c1728.name: sound_task
0x801c1728.evidence: the record the two servicers in game_main's frame poll: 0x80018cd0 acts when its +0 is 0x40 and its +0x10 is 1, 0x80015a48 when they are 0x30 and 2. 0x8001a438 sets it up and 0x8001967c advances it

0x800357e8.name: view_pose_set
0x800357e8.evidence: copies the camera pose render_frame is given into player_pos_view and its three angles, and divides the X and Z by 2048 into 0x801aec64 and 0x801aec68 -- the cell the camera is in. First stage of render_frame

0x800351fc.name: texture_scroll_step
0x800351fc.evidence: two 0x18-byte records at 0x801aeb1c, each a countdown, a scroll offset and a rect, advanced with MoveImage inside VRAM. The animated water and lava surfaces

0x80041f9c.name: message_tick
0x80041f9c.evidence: a state machine on 0x801aeaf7 over the byte sequence at 0x801aeaed indexed by 0x801aeaf5, drawing through 0x800277c0 -- the on-screen banner queue, with 0x19 taking its own path

0x80034bf4.name: view_matrix_build
0x80034bf4.evidence: three game_cos/game_sin pairs on the view angles at 0x801aec5c, folded by octant, into the scratchpad at 0x1f800118 and 0x801aec6c..0x78. The camera's rotation matrix for the frame

0x80035630.name: frame_begin_3d
0x80035630.evidence: flips draw_buffer_index, points current_draw_slot and ot_pointer at that buffer's records, and clears the 0x2000-entry ordering table with ClearOTagR plus an 8-entry one at 0x801a9178. The world's frame setup; frame_begin (0x80026fe4) is the menus' own

0x80043858.name: effect_timers_step
0x80043858.evidence: counts down the twelve bytes at 0x801aab64, stepping 0x14 apart, and clamps each at 1. Nothing else writes them

0x8003df50.name: draw_held_item
0x8003df50.evidence: returns at once when 0x801b25a4 is -1. Otherwise it takes the lighting of the cell the player stands in -- tile_look + 108 * (cell & 0x3f), which is what fixes tile_look's stride at 108 -- loads it into the GTE's light and colour matrices, and draws the model at 0x801b2594 with its own rotation. The thing in the player's hand

0x8003c35c.name: draw_model_cell_lit
0x8003c35c.evidence: the third model draw beside draw_model_lit and draw_model_plain: MVMVA, ScaleMatrix and the tile_look lighting, called once from render_frame between the held item and the terrain

0x8003bfd0.name: draw_terrain
0x8003bfd0.evidence: the cell walk: reads player_pos_view, block_copies the cells around it and calls draw_tile for each. render_frame's world pass

0x8003d280.name: overlay_plane_18
0x8003d280.evidence: reads depth_under_plane_18 -- how far the eye is under the surface collision opcode 0x18 places -- and fills the screen with it. One of three, one per plane

0x8003d38c.name: overlay_plane_19
0x8003d38c.evidence: the same for depth_under_plane_19, opcode 0x19's plane

0x8003d41c.name: overlay_plane_17
0x8003d41c.evidence: the same for the third depth at 0x801b2640, opcode 0x17's plane -- which is why that address was named camera_height, from where it is formed rather than from what it means

0x80035700.name: frame_end_3d
0x80035700.evidence: DrawSync, PutDispEnv and PutDrawEnv for the buffer draw_buffer_index names, then DrawOTag on its ordering table. The last drawing call of a frame

0x80043940.name: resource_sweep
0x80043940.evidence: the last call in render_frame: walks whatever free_object_resource is given and releases it

0x801b25a4.name: held_item_model
0x801b25a4.evidence: -1 when the player's hands are empty; draw_held_item returns immediately on that and otherwise draws the model at 0x801b2594

0x801b2594.name: held_item_record
0x801b2594.evidence: draw_held_item reads its +0x34..+0x38 as a position and +0x3c as a rotation, and hands the rotation to 0x80076168

0x80047010.name: object_interpreter
0x80047010.evidence: the third call in every frame and the largest routine in the game. Walks all 396 slots of object_table; per slot it publishes the record at 0x80198394 and object_type_table + 24*record[+6] at 0x80198390, skips a record whose +4 is 0xff, and switches on that byte through the 236-arm table at 0x8001209c -- 44 targets, of which two are not handlers: 0x8004b4b4, which 191 opcodes reach, calls level_hooks+0x24 -- the level's own code -- and 0x8004b4d0 is the loop's continue, which is where 0xe5 and 0xe9 go. Byte +4 is a copy of byte +0 of the type's row, which is the same class render_walk draws on. tools/objops.py maps it

0x8001209c.name: object_op_table
0x8001209c.evidence: 236 arms for object_interpreter's switch at 0x800470bc, guarded by `sltiu $v0, $v1, 0xec` on the object's class byte

0x80198394.name: current_object
0x80198394.evidence: object_interpreter writes the record it is running before dispatching, so every arm can find it without an argument

0x80198390.name: current_object_type
0x80198390.evidence: the same for object_type_table + 24 * record[+6], the type's own 24-byte row

0x8004482c.name: object_sound
0x8004482c.evidence: (record, kind) -> sound_cue_at(kind, record + 0x14, 0x78, 0). record+0x14 is the object's world position, so this is a cue played where the object stands. Nearly every arm of the object interpreter calls it

0x80015654.name: sound_cue_at
0x80015654.evidence: (kind, position, range, flags) -- what object_sound is a wrapper for, and what sound_play_3d sits under

0x80046884.name: player_in_rect
0x80046884.evidence: (cx, cz, w, h): true when the player's own cell -- player_pos >> 11 and 0x801b25f8 >> 11 -- lies inside the rectangle. The trigger test every door, teleport and switch in the object interpreter uses

0x80046914.name: object_use_state
0x80046914.evidence: switches on the object's +8, the interaction state, and gives up when its +0x38 is 0xff. The handler the opcodes that need a use call

0x801baa2e.name: script_speaker
0x801baa2e.evidence: the script record's +1, written by opcode 0xf6 and at the top of script_interpreter when the state's +0x10 is zero; the interpreter compares it with the record's +1 to decide whether to skip to the next 0xf0

0x8018fae0.name: level_hooks
0x8018fae0.evidence: a pointer to a structure of function pointers. level_load points it at 0x8007e4e4; level_overlay_tick calls its +4 once a frame and a script's 0xf4 opcode calls its +0x10. Whether it is the same table tools/overlay.py lists as the level's entry points is not established

0x8002ab18.name: player_take_hit
0x8002ab18.evidence: (slash, blow, stab, dark, holy, fire, earth, wind, water, scale, percent, kind) -- nine attack values, one per damage type, the same nine tools/player.py reads. Each goes through damage_of_type against the matching defence rating; the nine are summed, scaled by arg9 as (arg9*sum + 0x8000) >> 16 and by arg10 as (arg10*that)/10, and handed to apply_damage. Both scales are 0x1000 and 0xa at the call site 0x8004d358. Checked: 6 of 6 hits in out/lua_bp20.log reproduced exactly by tools/damage.py, and the seventh -- the kill -- comes out at 59 against 33 HP

0x8002a5f8.name: damage_of_type
0x8002a5f8.evidence: (stat, defence, attack) -> the damage of one type. A = attack*16, D = ((stat * [0x801b24f8]) >> 8) + defence*16, and the answer is (max(0, A - D) + A*A/(2*D)) / 5, with D forced to 0x10 when it is zero and 0 returned when the attack is. So a hit gets through in two ways at once and the quadratic term never quite vanishes

0x8002a6f4.name: apply_damage
0x8002a6f4.evidence: subtracts the damage from player_hp and clamps; the only place the player's HP goes down in combat

0x801b2524.name: player_stat_effective
0x801b2524.evidence: the effective copy of player_stat_36 that sub_80029500 writes each time the ratings are recomputed; damage_of_type scales the defence by it. 20 at level 1

0x801b24f8.name: damage_scale
0x801b24f8.evidence: a halfword, 0x1000 in every snapshot; damage_of_type multiplies the stat by it and shifts right 8

0x8002b468.name: new_character
0x8002b468.evidence: level 1, experience 0, and HP max, MP max and player_stat_36 straight out of level_table's first row; all five growth stats from level_table + 6, which is zero; gold zero and the four equipment slots 0xff. player_controller calls it on death when the player has no item 107, together with reset_story_flags -- so dying without the crystal is a new character

0x801b2520.name: player_growth_stat
0x801b2520.evidence: the last of the five halfwords award_exp rolls for, and in practice the only live one: new_character seeds all five from level_table + 6, which is 0, and a level-1 snapshot has [0,0,0,0,10]. award_exp skips a stat that is zero, so four of the five never grow. sub_8002a10c and use_item also write it
